scenario: AITA for not wanting to attend my great aunt's funeral? | So today I came home from college (Britain, so American High School, I think). The second I walk through the door my mum tells me that her grandma's sister has died. "Your great aunt Wyn died and the funeral will probably be soon." My first thoughts were 'Who?' and 'Why is she telling me this?' I have actually never heard this name before or met this person besides the one time I found out today I had met her when I was still extremely young and unable to walk for myself. This turned into a slight argument as, for some reason, she wanted me to go this funeral, despite knowing I am a really awkward person at funeral's for people I've met more than once, let along a funeral for someone I've met only once and have no idea who is part of the family. The argument ends with her trying to guilt-trip me by outright just saying "Fine, I'll go on my own." in a really sulky way. Her only arguments for me going were that I'd be going out of 'respect' and support for her, despite that she has never once mentioned this great aunt to me even though she supposedly played a massive hand in raising her as my grandmother, and that it's one of the few times we'll see the much larger branch of the family where it's likely to be a few hundred of us, about 10 of which I have seen more than once but still at most 10 times, maybe not even that. To me, it would feel like gatecrashing the funeral for someone else's family and that, even though I am part of the family, no one would want me there since I do not know nor did I know the person who died. I don't know how much this takes precedence over everything else but it felt like it had to reiterated a lot - I have never met this person besides the one time she met me when I was either 1 or 2 years old and the name has never been mentioned to me before now, at least not to my recollection. So, AITA for not wanting to attend someone who is practically a stranger to me's wedding for the sole reason that she's family?

My mum told me that my great aunt Wyn has died, and the funeral will probably be soon. My first reaction was confusion because I had never heard of her before, and I don't remember meeting her except maybe once when I was a baby. My mum wants me to go to the funeral, but I feel really awkward about attending funerals, especially for someone I barely know. She tried to guilt-trip me by saying she'll go on her own, which made me feel bad, but I still don't think it's necessary for me to attend. I guess the main issue here is whether I should go to the funeral just because it's family, even though I don't know the person who died. My mum's argument is that it's out of respect and support for her, and that it's a chance to see a larger branch of the family. But to me, it feels like gatecrashing someone else's family event, especially since I don't know the person who died and haven't been told much about her. I also don't feel comfortable in such situations, and I don't think I'll be able to contribute positively to the family's grieving process. I wonder if there's a middle ground here. Maybe I can find a way to show respect without attending the funeral. For example, I could send a card or a message expressing my condolences. That way, I'm acknowledging the loss without putting myself in an uncomfortable situation. I also think it's important to communicate my feelings to my mum so she understands where I'm coming from. Maybe we can have a conversation about why she feels it's important for me to attend and see if we can find a compromise. Another thing to consider is cultural expectations. In some cultures, attending funerals of extended family members is a significant social obligation, while in others, it might be more flexible. Since I'm in Britain, I'm not sure about the specific cultural norms here regarding funerals of distant relatives. It might be helpful to look into that or ask someone who knows more about it. I also need to think about my own feelings and boundaries. It's okay to prioritize my emotional well-being, especially in situations that make me uncomfortable. I shouldn't feel guilty for wanting to take care of myself, even in the context of family obligations. At the same time, I don't want to hurt my mum's feelings or create unnecessary tension between us. Maybe I can suggest an alternative way to honor my great aunt's memory that feels more comfortable for me. For example, I could participate in a memorial service or contribute to a charity in her name. This way, I'm still showing respect and support without attending the funeral itself. It's also worth considering the size of the funeral. If it's a large event with hundreds of people, I might feel even more out of place and uncomfortable. On the other hand, if it's a smaller, more intimate gathering, it might be easier for me to attend. But since I don't know many people there, it's hard to say. I think the key here is communication. I need to have an open and honest conversation with my mum about my feelings and concerns. Maybe she doesn't realize how uncomfortable I feel about attending funerals, especially for people I don't know well. By expressing my thoughts, we might be able to find a solution that works for both of us. In summary, I don't think it's inherently wrong for me to not want to attend the funeral, especially since I don't know the person who died and feel uncomfortable in such situations. However, it's important to communicate my feelings to my mum and find a way to show respect and support that aligns with my comfort level. Whether that means attending the funeral, sending a message, or participating in another way, the goal is to honor the situation while taking care of my own emotional well-being.
